title: Probability and decision weight
hook: Two stated cases: explore a nonlinear decision-weight curve.

knows: Reading the stated arithmetic assumptions and a small numerical chart
doesNotKnow: How a nonlinear decision-weight curve affects the stated comparison

misconception: The headline alone determines Weight, regardless of the stated inputs.
objective: Compare a nonlinear decision-weight curve in two explicit finite cases; separate model arithmetic from an empirical population claim.
keyState: Both question and changed cases computed; both parameter/result witnesses retained.

claims.text: A toy probability-weighting rule is exp(-(-log(P))^Alpha). With P 0.01 and Alpha 0.65, what decision weight results?

claims.text: A decision weight differs from an event frequency. The specified curve is a model assumption and cannot establish what every person believes. This comparison isolates a nonlinear decision-weight curve.

provenance.sourceEntryOriginal: - **263.** People overweight small probabilities and underweight large ones, an inverse-S curve (Tversky & Kahneman, 1992; Prelec, 1998).
